headline: Allowed more time for community outreach on proposed downtown parking changes, including tiered pricing and 95 metered spaces becoming free.

The presentation will go to councilors, neighborhood councils, and parking stakeholders for feedback, and the matter is expected on the October 19, 2026 City Council agenda.

Public Portion 
 1. Discussion on Parking Authority Presentation. 
 
Minutes: 
On September 28, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to 
review proposed changes to the downtown parking system. The committee reviewed a parking 
study examining utilization, pricing, revenue, enforcement, and Springfield Parking Authority 
facilities. The study identified approximately 12,000 parking spaces within the downtown study 
area, with approximately 4,000 under public control, and found that parking demand varies 
significantly by location. The study also identified underutilized parking facilities and financial 
challenges related to parking revenue and deferred maintenance. 
 
The committee reviewed proposed tiered pricing for on-street and garage parking based on 
location and demand. The proposal would increase rates in higher-demand areas, maintain or 
reduce rates in lower-demand areas, and convert approximately 95 currently metered spaces to 
free parking. The proposal also includes longer parking periods, potential expansion of paid 
parking hours, improved signage and payment options, updated parking equipment, and 
reinvestment of additional revenue into parking facilities and downtown improvements. The 
committee discussed the impact on residents, employees, businesses, garage users, enforcement, 
downtown activity, and the need for public education before implementation. 
 
The committee agreed to allow additional time for community outreach before bringing the 
proposed parking changes to the full City Council. The presentation will be distributed to City 
Councilors, and information will be shared with neighborhood councils and parking stakeholders 
for review and feedback. The matter is expected to be placed on the October 19, 2026 City 
Council agenda for consideration.
The meeting adjourned at 4:51 p.m.
